headline: Daily research brief — Sunday, October 4

items.detail: TSLA (Oct 21, company-confirmed), MSFT (~Oct 27-28, date unverified), AAPL (~Oct 29, date unverified), and NVDA (~Nov 17, cited but unverified) all sit inside the Oct-30 and Nov-20 expiries. Term structures hump over the events — MSFT 28-day IV 32.2% vs 7-day 22.6%, TSLA 43.5% vs 34.7%, AAPL 25.3% vs 20.9%, NVDA 49-day 34.2% vs 28-day 28.8%. These gaps are earnings-event pricing, not mispricings; premium into any of the four expiries is off-limits by the binary-event rule.
items.title: Binary-event premium dominates four of six names

items.detail: SPY's 30-day IV of 12.5% sits 2.4 points above its 20-day realized 10.1%, and the window is nearly clean — the largest single-day move contributed 29.4% of variance, just under the 30% window-contingency line. QQQ's wider 3.7-point gap is window-contingent: one stale Sep-21 day drove 41.9% of its 20-day variance, so wait for that day to roll out before re-reading it. Market volatility (VIX) closed Friday at 15.31, down 6.59%, with futures in contango — broad vol is not in a hedging regime.
items.title: SPY holds the only un-conflicted premium on the watchlist

items.detail: Monday brings ISM Services PMI; Tuesday the EIA outlook plus a $58B 3Y auction; Wednesday EIA petroleum data, a $39B 10Y auction, and the FOMC September-meeting minutes at 2:00 PM ET (release day verified against the Fed Board calendar); Thursday jobless claims and a $22B 30Y auction; Friday U-Mich sentiment and the October WASDE. The 10Y settled Friday at 5.277% after touching 5.34% intraweek — the highest since 2002. September CPI arrives Wednesday, October 14.
items.title: Macro-dense week inside front-month expiries; the 10Y touched a 24-year high

items.detail: No watchlist name goes ex-div between Oct 5 and Nov 1 (verified per name; Nov 1 is a non-trading day).
